title: GPU Nsight occupancy analysis - March 2026
content:
Summary:

This note captures the Nsight profiling runs and initial analysis for GPU utilization/occupancy regressions observed on the latest inference runtime (main @2026-03-05). We ran several Nsight Systems profiles and CUDA-graph experiments to understand why per-GPU throughput is ~18% below expected on A100 80GB (PCIe) under production-like traffic.

Test setup:
- HW: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 80GB (test cluster node), CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS 12.1, cuDNN 9.x.
- Software: serving-runtime branch perf-investigate/2026-03, custom kernel fusions off (baseline), CUDA graphs enabled in some runs.
- Model: llama-2-13b quantized (int8 fallback for some kernels), sequence length 512, typical batch sizes tested: 1, 4, 8, 16.
- Tools: Nsight Systems 2025.3 (nsys), Nsight Compute for kernel-level metrics, nvprof deprecated paths avoided.
- Files: nsys report files saved as "gpu-nsight-occupancy-2026-03-10-rep.nsys-rep" and "gpu-nsight-cudagraphs-2026-03-11-rep.nsys-rep" (linked above).

Observed symptoms:
- Average SM utilization across A100 is low: 24% for batch=1, 46% for batch=8, 58% for batch=16.
- Several short-lived kernels dominate wall time (many <50us launches) creating high launch overhead and poor occupancy.
- Notable kernels with high cumulative time: attention_matmul (cuBLAS Lt GEMM kernels), scaled_softmax (custom CUDA kernel), kv_cache_write, and small elementwise kernels used for rotary/positioning.
- Frequent host-device synchronizations visible in timeline: periodic cudaMemcpy + stream synchronizations triggered by logging/latency-measure hooks in the runtime.
- CUDA graph runs reduce CPU overhead but did not materially increase SM occupancy for small batch sizes; improvement is visible only when we fuse sequences (batch >=8) or increase sequence length.

Key Nsight timeline findings:
- Timeline shows micro-kernels pattern: ~2000 kernel launches per request for seq=512,batch=1. Kernel launch overhead accumulates and stalls GPU progress.
- Kernel durations are too short to saturate SMs; warp occupancy and active warps per SM are often <40%.
- Memory throughput is well under GPU peak (30-40% of theoretical), suggesting compute underutilization is primary issue rather than memory bandwidth.
- Several kernels fall back to non-tensor-core paths (FP32) in mixed-precision runs due to tensor alignment / stride shapes not satisfying tensorcore-friendly sizes.

Hypotheses and root-cause candidates:
1) Small kernel shapes & many launches: Transformer micro-op decomposition yields many small GEMMs and elementwise kernels causing launch overhead and low arithmetic intensity.
2) Kernel implementations not using Tensor Cores consistently: either data layout or batch dims are too small for cublasLt auto-tuning to pick tensor-core paths.
3) CPU-side stalls / synchronization: logging and synchronous profiling hooks force stream syncs between subgraphs.
4) KV cache memory patterns causing inefficient global memory access (non-coalesced writes) leading to low effective occupancy on some kernels.
5) CUDA grid/block launch configuration (blockDim) suboptimal for our shapes (use occupancy calculator).

Investigations done so far:
- Nsight Compute on attention kernels shows low SM efficiency and low tensor-core utilization for many GEMMs; cublasLt heuristics selected TF32/FP32.
- Re-ran with enforced FP16 inputs and cuBLAS math mode set to allow tensor cores; saw 20-30% reduction in time for large GEMMs but small GEMMs still dominated by launch overhead.
- Enabled CUDA graphs for static graph segment (pre-allocated KV cache + generation loop). This reduced CPU-side overhead (~15% lower per-request CPU time) but improved GPU throughput only for batch >=8.
- Increased sequence length to 1024 in a controlled run: SM utilization improved to ~72% for batch=4, indicating sequence length increases arithmetic intensity and improves occupancy.
- Microbenchmark: fused attention (prototype kernel) shows 2x speedup on attention matmuls, but fusion introduces complexity and edge-cases for KV caching and variable sequence lengths.

Immediate recommendations:
- Short term (low risk):
  - Turn off synchronous logging hooks during hot-path inference; move logs to async buffers. (INF-4823)
  - Enable cuBLASLt heuristics to prefer tensor-core paths and enforce FP16 where safe (model eval with small eval set).
  - Increase default request batch target for Dedicated to 4 or more where latency SLO allows; add route-level batching config.

- Medium term (engineering work):
  - Implement persistent/fused attention kernel path (evaluate memory vs speed tradeoffs). Prototype suggests 1.8-2x improvement for our workload.
  - Add kernel launch coalescing / stream aggregation to reduce number of launches per request (group small elementwise kernels).
  - Add a tuning pass that inspects shapes at model load and selects optimized kernels or changes launch params to improve occupancy (use occupancy calculator heuristics).

- Long term (research/holistic):
  - Consider redesign of KV cache layout to be more coalesced-friendly for our write patterns.
  - Expand testbed to include A100-SXM4 and H100 nodes and ensure heuristics select kernel implementations per GPU architecture.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much variability in perf is due to PCIe vs NVLink node configuration? We only tested on PCIe nodes so far. Need NVLink baseline.
- For int8 quantized paths we saw regressions on some GEMMs — are the quant kernels falling back to slower reference implementations? Need to confirm with kernel-level tracing.
- Can we safely change default numeric type to FP16 for all customers? Need QA for potential small numeric diffs for some prompt classes.

Next steps (owners & tickets):
- Miguel: remove synchronous logging, add async logging branch, measure CPU/GPU impact (JIRA INF-4823). Target: 1 week.
- Noah: run NVLink vs PCIe comparison and add to report; capture Nsight runs for NVLink node (INF-4827). Target: 1 week.
- Lina: prototype kernel coalescing and occupancy tuning pass; build microbench harness and submit PR with perf numbers. Target: 2-3 weeks.

Notes to self (informal):
- Watch out for overfitting heuristics to llama-2 shapes — need generalizable rules for different model widths and k/v dims.
- Keep a copy of Nsight .nsys-rep in drive and tag with run parameters (batch, seq, model commit).

Attachments / artifacts: nsys reports and Nsight compute snippets saved in linked_artifacts. See "gpu-nsight-occupancy-2026-03-10-rep.nsys-rep" for the main timeline.

If reviewers want visuals: I can export the kernel timeline screenshots (png) and a small table of per-kernel metrics (time, launches, avg duration, SM-eff, tensor-core-usage).
